imageInfo.caption: Kilij Arslan I overseeing the heaping of the bones of the People's Crusade after Civetot, in an engraving by Vinzenz Katzler of about 1872.
imageInfo.creator: Vinzenz Katzler
imageInfo.note: A nineteenth-century European engraving, not a portrait and not sympathetic — it belongs to a tradition of orientalist crusade illustration and should be read as such. It replaces a locator map of the Sultanate of Rum, which depicted no person at all and is now the primary image of the sultanate's own article. The bone heap at Civetot is attested: Anna Komnene and the crusader chroniclers all describe it. Public domain.

overview: Kilij Arslan I was Seljuk sultan of Rum during the First Crusade. He destroyed the People’s Crusade but underestimated the main crusader armies that later crossed Anatolia.
His career shows the fractured political world that the First Crusade entered: Muslim rulers did not act as a single united bloc.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Kilij Arslan I was Seljuk sultan of Rum during the First Crusade. He destroyed the People’s Crusade but underestimated the main crusader armies that later crossed Anatolia.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Kilij Arslan inherited a sultanate in Anatolia formed after Manzikert and contested by Danishmendids, Byzantines, and crusaders.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Kilij Arslan I is remembered as the young and energetic Seljuk sultan of Rum who confronted the First Crusade as it cut across Anatolia, and the sources — chiefly Byzantine and crusader — present a bold but ultimately outmatched adversary. He had earlier destroyed the disorganised People's Crusade with ease, which may have led him to underestimate the disciplined main army that followed, allowing it to take his capital and defeat him in the field.

Recovering from these reverses, he proved a persistent and capable enemy of both the crusaders and the Byzantines, and later destroyed a subsequent crusading force, demonstrating that his early defeats had not broken him. The sources present a determined and adaptable ruler navigating the sudden, overwhelming pressure of the crusade and the rivalries among Muslim powers.

Because he is seen mainly through the eyes of his enemies, his individual character is only partly visible. What the record supports is a brave, resilient, and ambitious ruler who misjudged the First Crusade but recovered to defend and expand his sultanate. He is remembered as the Seljuk sultan who first met the crusaders in Anatolia — formidable, persistent, and shaped by that collision.

contentSections.title: As Seljuk sultan of Rum
paragraphs: He defeated the People’s Crusade near Civetot in 1096. In 1097, the main crusader armies and Byzantines took Nicaea, forcing him into mobile resistance across Anatolia.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Kilij Arslan drowned in the Khabur River in 1107 during conflict with rival Muslim powers.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: His career shows the fractured political world that the First Crusade entered: Muslim rulers did not act as a single united bloc.
